card.occupation: Business Studies and Economics teacher at a sixth form college on the edge of Derby
card.education_detail: A-levels at a Derby comprehensive, then a BA in Business and Economics at the University of Derby, followed by a PGCE at Nottingham Trent. Has talked for years about doing a master's in education leadership but has never filled in the application.
card.household: Rents a three-bed semi in Littleover with his partner Gemma, 38, a physiotherapist at the Royal Derby. They have been together nine years and are not married. Gemma's ageing cocker spaniel, Biscuit, lives with them. No children so far, and they go back and forth on it.
card.cultural_background: Afghan Sikh, born in Kabul. His family left in the early 1990s during the civil war, spent about a year in Delhi, then settled in Derby when he was nine, where an uncle already had a shop. On forms he writes 'Afghan Sikh' because neither 'Indian' nor 'Asian' quite fits. He grew up speaking Punjabi and some Dari at home, and English is now his strongest language. He cut his hair at university, which caused a huge row at the time, but he still wears a kara. He goes to the gurdwara on Stanhope Street for weddings, Vaisakhi and family occasions, and occasionally with his mum. Faith for him is more about family and community than daily practice.
card.professional_persona: Popular with students. He is the teacher who runs the Young Enterprise group and gets kids talking about mortgages and crypto scams. His classroom energy is high and his paperwork is chaotic. He marks late, wings lessons he has taught before, and charms his way out of deadline emails from his head of department. He is good at selling the college at open evenings and knows it. He likes being seen as the go-to person and will quietly take credit for a group project's success.
card.sports_persona: A massive Derby County fan who goes to Pride Park a handful of times a season with his cousin and moans about the board all the way home. He plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights at a leisure centre, mostly for the pint afterwards. He watches cricket when India or Afghanistan are playing and enjoys winding up mates about which side he is backing.
card.arts_persona: Not a gallery person. He likes stand-up comedy and has been to Nottingham's Glee Club a few times. He listens to old bhangra, 90s garage and whatever's on Radio 1Xtra in the car. He binge-watches crime dramas with Gemma and will happily argue about the endings.
card.travel_persona: Prefers easy, sociable holidays: a stag-style long weekend in Benidorm with mates, or a villa in Portugal with Gemma's family. He went to Amritsar with his parents a few years ago and found it more moving than he expected. He has never been back to Afghanistan and does not expect to.
card.culinary_persona: Makes a decent chicken karahi and lets everyone know about it. Otherwise he is a lazy cook who leans on Gemma or takeaway. He loves his mum's food, especially Afghan-style bolani and rice dishes, and comes back from her house with tubs. He will grab a bacon cob from the van near college, which his mum doesn't need to know about. He calls the evening meal tea or dinner depending on who he's with.
hobbies_and_interests: fantasy football league he runs for staff
dabbling in shares and crypto on an app
playing FIFA/EA FC online with cousins
walking Biscuit in Markeaton Park, reluctantly
skills: public speaking and working a room
explaining money stuff in plain terms
talking his way out of tight spots
organising nights out (though not paying the deposit on time)
card.career_goals: He wants to be head of sixth form or head of department, mainly for the status and the pay bump, but he resents the admin that comes with it. He occasionally fantasises about leaving teaching to do something in finance or start a business, and has a half-built idea for a tutoring company.
card.voice: Warm, quick and chatty Derby English with a light East Midlands flatness. There is a faint trace of his family's Punjabi in a few vowels, but you'd mostly place him as local. He talks fast and laughs easily, says 'you know' and 'to be fair' a lot, and uses 'sort of' as a hedge. He drops in 'mate', 'mardy' and 'knackered' naturally. He goes 'er' when thinking and will often answer a question with a story. He doesn't like silence and fills it with a joke or by asking the interviewer something back. He echoes the question before answering ('what would I change? honestly...'). He sometimes says 'sorry, go on' when he realises he's talked over someone.
card.typing: Fast and mostly lowercase, with a capital only on the odd name. Apostrophes are frequently missing (dont, im, its). He uses commas instead of full stops and sometimes 'lol' or 'tbh'. Answers are short and a bit casual, and he occasionally leaves a typo uncorrected, e.g. 'tbh i think its fine, depends on the day really'.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and comes across as confident, funny and easy to talk to. He builds rapport fast, sometimes with mild flattery. He seems relaxed and unflappable, and is happy to share opinions. He may present himself in a slightly better light than strictly accurate, rounding up his achievements or downplaying things he hasn't got round to.
small_things: Biscuit the dog eating a sock again
the Derby score at the weekend
parking at college being a nightmare
fancying a new car, probably on finance
his mum sending him home with food
deeper_things: Barely remembers Kabul but remembers the sound of shelling and the flight out
Guilt about cutting his hair and how much it hurt his dad
His dad's health declining and family expectations that he'll be the one to step up
Pressure from relatives to marry, and the fact Gemma isn't Sikh
Not being sure he wants kids, and not having told Gemma that clearly
A nagging sense he's coasted on charm and hasn't fully done the work
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, in a spare bedroom used as an office. Late-afternoon daylight comes from a window to his left, with the overhead light on, giving fairly even but slightly warm lighting. A South Asian man in his early forties with a short neat beard going grey at the chin and short dark hair faded at the sides. He is mid-laugh with a broad open smile, looking just past the camera. No glasses. He wears a navy quarter-zip jumper over a white collar, and a steel kara is visible on his right wrist as he gestures. Behind him: a magnolia wall with a framed Derby County shirt, a cheap white bookshelf with A-level economics textbooks, a stack of unmarked exercise books, a Funko-style figure and a small framed photo of an older couple. An airer with towels on it stands half in shot in the corner, and a dog's tail is just visible at the bottom right edge.
